title: A2-09 · L'iḍāfa with adjectives and chains of iḍāfa

blocks.text: A2-09 · L'iḍāfa with adjectives and chains of iḍāfa
Lesson overview

L'iḍāfa (A1-10) is the most frequent construction of the institutional language: ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ , ⁧وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ . In titles and documents it extends in chains of three or four names ( ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ لَجْنَةِ الشُّؤُونِ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ ) and combines with adjectives that all go to the bottom. In this unit you learn to build and above all to unmount these chains, to use the duals and the healthy plurals inside theiḍāfa and the quantifiers are each, all, some, the same, most of them. The vocabulary is that of the organigrams: who directs what. A week.

rows: A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase
6–7 hours · one week (week 64 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-09), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. build and analyse chains of iḍāfa of three and four names;
2. place the adjective at the bottom of the chain and understand what name it refers to;
3. use the male dual and plural healthy as the first term ( ⁧مُوَظَّفُو الوِزَارَةِ⁩ , ⁧وَزِيرَا الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ );
4. use ⁧كُلّ⁩ , ⁧بَعْض⁩ , ⁧جَمِيع⁩ , ⁧مُعْظَم⁩ , ⁧نَفْس⁩ , ⁧غَيْر⁩ , ⁧عِدَّة⁩ with the right case and determination;
5. read an organization chart and unvoiceless institutional titles and present an institution in 80 words.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧نَائِبُ مُدِيرِ الإِدَارَةِ⁩ and ⁧مَكْتَبُ رَئِيسِ قِسْمِ شُؤُونِ الأَجَانِبِ⁩ are chains: only the last name has the article, all names after the first one are at the genitive. In ⁧رَئِيسَةُ قِسْمِ الجَوَازَاتِ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ the adjective is at the bottom but refers to the first name (female, nominative). ⁧مُتَرْجِمُو المَكْتَبِ⁩ The translators of the office are: ⁧مُتَرْجِمَا اللُّغَةِ⁩ The two translators of the language have lost the ⁧ن⁩ (Section 3). ⁧كُلُّ المُوَظَّفِينَ⁩ • all employees • ⁧جَمِيعَ الأَقْسَامِ⁩ • all sections • ⁧مُعْظَمُهُمْ⁩ • most of them • ⁧بَعْضُهُمْ⁩ Some of them (section) 4). ⁧مَمَرّ⁩ It is in the vocabulary.
2. Chains of iḍāfa
A chain is a series of iḍāfa One inside the other. The Rules of A1-10 apply to each ring:
1. only the last name can have the article (or be a proper name, or have a suffix pronoun);
2. all names except the first one are at the genitive;
3. the first name has the case that gives it its function in the sentence;
4. no name of the chain, except the last one, has the article or the tanwīn;
5. the last name decides whether the whole chain is determined or not.

rows: the office of the director of the company
the door of the company's director's office

blocks.text: ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ شَرِكَةٍ⁩ ... + of a company (undetermined) the office of the director of a company

How to dismount a chain without vowels. Read from right: the first name without article opens the chain; any name without the following article is a new ring; the first name with the article (or a proper name, or a suffix pronoun) closes it. ⁧مكتب مدير الشركة: مكتب⁩ (opens) ⁧مدير⁩ (Ring) ⁧الشركة⁩ (closes). The tāʾ marbūṭa Inside the chain we read -at: ⁧سَيَّارَةُ مُدِيرَةِ المَدْرَسَةِ⁩ sayyāratu mudīrati I-madrasa.
3. Adjectives and chains
An adjective cannot enter the chain: it is put at the bottom, after the last name, and agrees (genre, number, case, determination) with the name to which it refers.

rows: the new car of the director
the car of the new director
the large office of the section head

blocks.text: ⁧رَئِيسَةرَئِيسَةُ القِسْمِ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ (f., no.) the new chapter of the section

If the two names have the same kind and the chain is long, only the desinences say what name the adjective refers to: ⁧مُدِيرُ المَكْتَبِ الجَدِيدُ⁩ (the Director is new) / ⁧مُدِيرُ المَكْتَبِ الجَدِيدِ⁩ (the office is new). In texts without vowels, ambiguity remains, and often only solves the context: when you translate, it points out doubts rather than choosing at random (it is a professional habit that you will develop in the INT module). Two adjectives for two different names: first that of the last name, then that of the first one (the order is "mirror"): ⁧وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ المِصْرِيَّةِ السَّابِقُ⁩ The former Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs (Lett. The former Minister of Foreign Policy of Egypt). Alternative without iḍāfa: the purpose with ⁧لِـ⁩ . To avoid ambiguity or too long chains modern Arabic often uses ⁧لِـ⁩ : ⁧مُدِيرٌ جَدِيدٌ لِلْمَكْتَبِ⁩ A new Director of the Office (undetermined), ⁧زِيَارَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ لِلْوَزِيرِ⁩ A formal visit by the Minister.
4. Dual and plural healthy iniḍāfa
When a male dual or plural healthy is the first term of aiḍāfa (or takes a suffix pronoun), loses the ⁧ن⁩ final:
plural healthy m., nominative ⁧مُوَظَّفُوهُمُوَظَّفُو الوِزَارَةِمُوَظَّفُونَ⁩
• ⁧اِجْتَمَعَ وَزِيرَا الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ The two Foreign Ministers met;
• ⁧تَكَلَّمْتُ مَعَ مُوَظَّفِي البَنْكِ⁩ I spoke to the bank employees.

In front of the article the final long vowels -ā, -ū, -ī they write (and in the transliteration remain long), but in the pronunciation they shorten, as in ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ : wazīrā l-ḫāriǧiyya is pronounced [wazīra l-ḫāriǧiyya], muwaẓẓafū l- wizāra [muwaẓẓafu l-wizāra], muwaẓẓafī l-bank [muwaẓẓafi I-bank). The diphthong -ay takes a support instead: wazīrayi l-ḫāriǧiyya. In texts without vowels these plurals are recognizable by ⁧و⁩ or by ⁧ي⁩ the final text followed by: ⁧موظفو الوزارة⁩ , ⁧موظفي البنك⁩ . The alif muta of ⁧دَرَسُوا⁩ ( A2-02) does not include these names: ⁧مُوَظَّفُو⁩ , not * ⁧مُوَظَّفُوا⁩ . The healthy female plural does not change: ⁧مُوَظَّفَاتُ الوِزَارَةِ⁩ .
5. Quantifiers
"Every, all, some, most, same, other are names that make from the first term of a'iḍāfa.

6. Pronunciation

The chains are all in one breath. Inside the chain there are no breaks: maktabu mudīri š-šarika, with the vowels of the genitive -i that bind words. The break only falls in the end. -at of tāʾ marbūṭa. madīnatu Mīlānū, raʾīsatu l-qism, wizāratu d-dāḫiliyya: every ⁧ة⁩ Inside the chain you feel like t. Dual and plural before the article. wazīra l-ḫāriǧiyya, muwaẓẓafu l-wizāra, muwaẓẓafī l-bank: the long written vowel shortens, but remains of clear stamp.

11. Writing
Exercise 11 · Presenting an entity

Write about 80 vocalized words to present an agency you know (your office, your school, an association, a company): what is it called, where it is located, which offices and sections it has, who directs them (invented names), how many people work there, what do they do. Required elements: at least four chains of iḍāfa (two of three names); two adjectives at the bottom of a chain; a healthy plural or a dual in iḍāfa; Three different quantizers.
